audience.text: Python developers building 3D content pipelines, especially in 3D printing, CAD, and visualization workflows requiring format conversion and scene graph manipulation.

capabilities.text: Read OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB, COLLADA, and 3MF files using Scene.open() with automatic format detection or explicit FileFormat specification.
capabilities.title: Import multiple 3D formats

capabilities.text: Write scenes to OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB, and 3MF using Scene.save() with format-specific SaveOptions for compression, coordinate flipping, and unit scaling.
capabilities.title: Export to common 3D formats

capabilities.text: Build meshes from control points and polygons, convert primitives to meshes, and triangulate arbitrary polygon data.
capabilities.title: Construct and edit mesh geometry

capabilities.text: Attach LambertMaterial or PbrMaterial to nodes and set diffuse, albedo, metallic, and roughness properties directly.
capabilities.title: Assign and configure materials

capabilities.text: Compose hierarchical scenes using Node.create_child_node(), Node.add_entity(), and Node.child_nodes with independent transforms per node.
capabilities.title: Build and traverse scene graphs

capabilities.text: Create animation clips with AnimationClip, AnimationNode, and KeyframeSequence, and store skeletal bind-pose data with Pose.
capabilities.title: Support keyframe animation

limitations.text: FBX export is not implemented; FbxExporter.save() and save_to_stream() raise NotImplementedError.
COLLADA export is not reachable through Scene.save() due to exporter lookup order issues.
Scene.render() and the entire aspose.threed.render module raise NotImplementedError.
Texture construction raises NotImplementedError; image-backed textures cannot be created.
Mesh boolean operations (union, difference, intersect) raise NotImplementedError.
NURBS curve evaluation and surface-to-mesh conversion raise NotImplementedError.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic conversion between common 3D formats (OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB, COLLADA, 3MF) using a consistent Scene/Node/Mesh API.
Provides a pure-Python implementation with no external SDK or native runtime dependency, simplifying deployment across Windows, macOS, and Linux.
Supports building and editing 3D geometry from scratch using primitives, control points, and polygon construction.
Enables material assignment and scene graph traversal for 3D scene composition and inspection.

product_summary.text: Aspose.3D FOSS for Python is a pure-Python, MIT-licensed library for loading, constructing, and exporting 3D scenes without native dependencies.

uncertainties: The exact set of formats supported beyond the documented ones (OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB, COLLADA, 3MF) is not fully clarified; FBX import is marked experimental with limited verification.
Whether the public API surface beyond the listed public symbols is stable or complete is not confirmed by the facts.
The behavior of Scene.open() when no extension is present and no FileFormat is provided is not documented in the facts.
The status of animation export (e.g., to glTF with animations) is not explicitly verified in the examples or limitations.

workflows.name: Scene import and inspection
workflows.text: Load a 3D file using Scene.open() and inspect its geometry, nodes, and materials.

workflows.name: Scene export to common formats
workflows.text: Save a constructed or modified scene to OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB, or 3MF using Scene.save() with format-specific options.

workflows.name: Primitive-based geometry construction
workflows.text: Create parameterized primitives like Box or Sphere, convert them to editable meshes via to_mesh(), and attach materials.

workflows.name: Manual mesh construction
workflows.text: Build meshes vertex-by-vertex using Mesh.control_points and Mesh.create_polygon(), then attach to nodes.

workflows.name: Material assignment
workflows.text: Assign LambertMaterial or PbrMaterial to nodes and configure diffuse, albedo, metallic, and roughness properties.

workflows.name: Scene graph traversal
workflows.text: Navigate the scene graph using Node.create_child_node(), Node.child_nodes, and Node.entity to inspect or modify hierarchy.
